title: Entanglement Before Spacetime in Quantum-Gravity-Induced Interactions
summary: Quantum-gravity-induced entanglement of massive systems (QGEM) is commonly approximated in the nonrelativistic static limit by a Newtonian interaction between spatially separated masses. In this work, we reformulate the gravitationally mediated interaction phase in a conformally invariant twistor framework in which no notion of spacetime distance is assumed. We show that the bilocal phase responsible for entanglement generation remains well-defined and non-factorizable even in the absence of spacetime geometry. The familiar Newtonian $1/r$ phase, relevant for QGEM protocols, arises only after the conformal invariance is broken by introducing the infinity twistor, which selects a particular spacetime representation of the underlying bilocal quantum interaction. Our results isolate the genuinely quantum content of QGEM protocols and clarify the contingent role played by spacetime geometry in mediating entanglement.

AI.tldr: QGEM entanglement phase reformulated in conformally invariant twistor framework without spacetime distance; Newtonian 1/r phase emerges only after conformal symmetry breaking via infinity twistor.
AI.motivation: To isolate the genuinely quantum content of QGEM protocols by reformulating gravitationally mediated interaction in a framework that doesn't assume spacetime geometry, clarifying the contingent role of spacetime in mediating entanglement.
AI.method: Reformulate the gravitationally mediated interaction phase in a conformally invariant twistor framework that doesn't assume spacetime distance; analyze how the Newtonian 1/r phase emerges only after breaking conformal invariance via the infinity twistor.
AI.result: The bilocal phase responsible for entanglement generation remains well-defined and non-factorizable even without spacetime geometry; the familiar Newtonian 1/r phase arises only after conformal invariance is broken by introducing the infinity twistor.
AI.conclusion: The work isolates the genuinely quantum content of QGEM protocols and clarifies that spacetime geometry plays a contingent rather than fundamental role in mediating entanglement between massive systems.

title: Quantum-controlled synthetic materials
summary: Analog quantum simulators and digital quantum computers are two distinct paradigms driving near-term applications in modern quantum science, from probing many-body phenomena to identifying computational advantage over classical systems. A transformative opportunity on the horizon is merging the high-fidelity many-body evolution in analog simulators with the robust control and measurement of digital machines. Such a hybrid platform would unlock new capabilities in state preparation, characterization and dynamical control. Here, we embed digital quantum control in the analog evolution of a synthetic quantum material by entangling the lattice potential landscape of a Bose-Hubbard circuit with an ancilla qubit. This Hamiltonian-level control induces dynamics under a superposition of different lattice configurations and guides the many-body system to novel strongly-correlated states where different phases of matter coexist -- ordering photons into superpositions of solid and fluid eigenstates. Leveraging hybrid control modalities, we adiabatically introduce disorder to localize the photons into an entangled cat state and enhance its coherence using a many-body echo technique. This work illustrates the potential for entangling quantum computers with quantum matter -- synthetic and solid-state -- for advantage in sensing and materials characterization.

AI.tldr: Hybrid quantum platform merges analog simulator evolution with digital quantum control via ancilla qubit entanglement, enabling superposition of lattice configurations and creation of novel strongly-correlated states with coexisting phases.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between analog quantum simulators (high-fidelity many-body evolution) and digital quantum computers (robust control/measurement) by creating a hybrid platform that unlocks new capabilities in state preparation, characterization, and dynamical control of quantum materials.
AI.method: Embed digital quantum control in analog evolution of a Bose-Hubbard circuit by entangling the lattice potential landscape with an ancilla qubit, enabling Hamiltonian-level control that induces dynamics under superposition of different lattice configurations.
AI.result: Achieved Hamiltonian-level control guiding many-body system to novel strongly-correlated states where different phases of matter coexist, ordering photons into superpositions of solid and fluid eigenstates. Implemented adiabatic disorder introduction to localize photons into entangled cat states and enhanced coherence using many-body echo technique.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates potential for entangling quantum computers with quantum matter (synthetic and solid-state) for advantage in sensing and materials characterization, illustrating a transformative hybrid quantum platform.

title: Quantum simulation of the Dicke model in a two-dimensional ion crystal: chaos, quantum thermalization, and revivals
summary: Quantum many-body systems driven far from equilibrium can exhibit chaos, entanglement, and non-classical correlations, yet directly observing these phenomena in large, closed quantum systems remains challenging. Here we realize the Dicke model -- a fundamental description of light-matter interactions -- in a two-dimensional crystal of approximately 100 trapped ions. The ions' internal state is optically coupled to the center of mass vibrational mode via an optical spin-dependent force, enabling unitary many-body dynamics beyond the mean-field and few-body limits. In the integrable regime, where the phonons can be adiabatically eliminated, we observe a dynamical phase transition between ferromagnetic to paramagnetic spin phases. In contrast, when the spins and phonons are strongly coupled, we observe clear signatures of non-integrable chaotic dynamics, including erratic phase-space trajectories and the exponential growth of excitations and entanglement quantified by the one-body Rényi entropy. By quenching from an unstable fixed point in the near-integrable regime, quantum noise can generate correlated spin-phonon excitations. Our numerical calculations, in clear agreement with experiment, reveal the generation of two-mode spin-phonon squeezing, 2.6 dB below the standard quantum limit (4.6 dB relative to the initial thermal state), followed by generalized vacuum Rabi collapses and revivals. Our results establish large ion crystals as scalable analog quantum simulators of non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics and provide a controlled platform for experimental studies of information scrambling and entanglement in closed many-body systems.

AI.tldr: Experimental realization of Dicke model in 100-ion crystal demonstrates integrable dynamical phase transitions and non-integrable chaotic dynamics with entanglement growth and spin-phonon squeezing.
AI.motivation: Direct observation of chaos, entanglement, and non-classical correlations in large closed quantum systems is challenging. The Dicke model provides a fundamental description of light-matter interactions that can reveal these phenomena.
AI.method: Realized Dicke model in 2D crystal of ~100 trapped ions using optical spin-dependent force coupling internal states to center-of-mass vibrational mode. Studied both integrable (phonons adiabatically eliminated) and non-integrable (strong spin-phonon coupling) regimes.
AI.result: In integrable regime: observed dynamical phase transition between ferromagnetic and paramagnetic spin phases. In non-integrable regime: observed chaotic signatures including erratic phase-space trajectories, exponential growth of excitations and entanglement (quantified by one-body Rényi entropy). Achieved 2.6 dB spin-phonon squeezing below SQL (4.6 dB relative to initial thermal state) with vacuum Rabi collapses/revivals.
AI.conclusion: Large ion crystals serve as scalable analog quantum simulators for non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics, providing controlled platform for studying information scrambling and entanglement in closed many-body systems.

title: U(1) lattice gauge theory and string roughening on a triangular Rydberg array
summary: Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) describe fundamental interactions in particle physics. A central phenomenon in these theories is confinement, which binds quarks and antiquarks into hadrons through the formation of string-like flux tubes of gauge fields. Simulating confinement dynamics is a challenging task, but recent advances in quantum simulation are enabling the exploration of LGTs in regimes beyond the reach of classical computation. For analog devices, a major difficulty is the realization of strong plaquette interactions, which generate string fluctuations that can drive a roughening transition. Understanding string roughening -- where strong transversal functions lead to an effective restoration of translational symmetry at long distances -- is of central importance in the study of confinement. In this work, we show that string roughening emerges naturally in an analog Rydberg quantum simulator. We first map a triangular Rydberg array onto a (2+1)D U(1) LGT where plaquette terms appear as first-order processes. We study flux strings connecting static charges and demonstrate that, near a deconfined quantum critical point, the string exhibits logarithmic growth of its transverse width as the separation between charges increases, along with the universal Lüscher correction to the confining potential -- both signatures of string roughening. Finally, we investigate the real-time dynamics of an initially rigid string, observing large fluctuations after quenching into the roughening regime, as well as string breaking via particle-pair creation. Our results indicate that rough strings can be realized in experimentally accessible quantum simulators, opening the door to detailed studies of how strong fluctuations influence string-breaking dynamics.

AI.tldr: Rydberg quantum simulator naturally exhibits string roughening in U(1) lattice gauge theory, showing logarithmic width growth and Lüscher corrections near deconfined critical point.
AI.motivation: Understanding confinement dynamics in lattice gauge theories is challenging but crucial for particle physics. String roughening, where strong transversal fluctuations restore translational symmetry at long distances, is central to confinement studies but difficult to simulate classically. Quantum simulators offer new opportunities to explore these phenomena beyond classical computational limits.
AI.method: Map triangular Rydberg array onto (2+1)D U(1) lattice gauge theory where plaquette terms appear as first-order processes. Study flux strings connecting static charges near deconfined quantum critical point. Investigate real-time dynamics of initially rigid strings after quenching into roughening regime.
AI.result: String exhibits logarithmic growth of transverse width with charge separation and universal Lüscher correction to confining potential - both signatures of string roughening. Large fluctuations observed after quenching into roughening regime, along with string breaking via particle-pair creation. Rough strings can be realized in experimentally accessible quantum simulators.
AI.conclusion: String roughening emerges naturally in analog Rydberg quantum simulators, enabling detailed studies of how strong fluctuations influence string-breaking dynamics in lattice gauge theories, opening new avenues for exploring confinement physics beyond classical computational limits.

title: Warm Starts, Cold States: Exploiting Adiabaticity for Variational Ground-States
summary: Reliable preparation of many-body ground states is an essential task in quantum computing, with applications spanning areas from chemistry and materials modeling to quantum optimization and benchmarking. A variety of approaches have been proposed to tackle this problem, including variational methods. However, variational training often struggle to navigate complex energy landscapes, frequently encountering suboptimal local minima or suffering from barren plateaus. In this work, we introduce an iterative strategy for ground-state preparation based on a stepwise (discretized) Hamiltonian deformation. By complementing the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) with adiabatic principles, we demonstrate that solving a sequence of intermediate problems facilitates tracking the ground-state manifold toward the target system, even as we scale the system size. We provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for this approach, proving a lower bound on the loss variance that suggests trainability throughout the deformation, provided the system remains away from gap closings. Numerical simulations, including the effects of shot noise, confirm that this path-dependent tracking consistently converges to the target ground state.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an iterative ground-state preparation method combining VQE with adiabatic principles via Hamiltonian deformation to overcome variational training limitations.
AI.motivation: Variational methods for ground-state preparation often struggle with complex energy landscapes, encountering local minima and barren plateaus, necessitating more robust approaches.
AI.method: An iterative strategy based on stepwise Hamiltonian deformation that complements VQE with adiabatic principles, solving a sequence of intermediate problems to track the ground-state manifold.
AI.result: Theoretical proof of a lower bound on loss variance ensuring trainability away from gap closings, with numerical simulations (including shot noise) showing consistent convergence to target ground states.
AI.conclusion: The Hamiltonian deformation approach provides a reliable method for ground-state preparation that scales with system size and overcomes limitations of standard variational training.

title: Theory of direct measurement of the quantum pseudo-distribution via its characteristic function
summary: We propose a method for directly measuring the quantum mechanical pseudo-distribution of observable properties via its characteristic function. Vandermonde matrices of the eigenvalues play a central role in the theory. This proposal directly finds the pseudo-distribution using weak measurements of the generator of position moments (momentum translations). While the pseudo-distribution can be extracted from the data in a theory-agnostic way, it is shown that under quantum-mechanical formalism, the predicted pseudo-distribution is identified with the Kirkwood-Dirac pseudo-distribution. We discuss the construction of both the joint pseudo-distribution and a conditional pseudo-distribution, which is closely connected to weak-value physics. By permuting position and momentum measurements, we give a prescription to directly probe the canonical commutation relation and verify it for any quantum state. This work establishes the theory of a characteristic function approach to pseudo-distributions, as well as providing a constructive approach to measuring them directly.

AI.tldr: Direct measurement of quantum pseudo-distributions via characteristic functions using weak measurements of momentum translations, connecting to Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and weak values.
AI.motivation: To develop a direct experimental method for measuring quantum pseudo-distributions of observable properties, which are mathematically described but not directly measurable using conventional approaches.
AI.method: Uses characteristic function approach with Vandermonde matrices of eigenvalues; employs weak measurements of the generator of position moments (momentum translations) to directly extract pseudo-distributions in a theory-agnostic way.
AI.result: The measured pseudo-distribution is identified with the Kirkwood-Dirac pseudo-distribution under quantum formalism; enables construction of both joint and conditional pseudo-distributions; provides prescription to directly probe canonical commutation relations for any quantum state.
AI.conclusion: Establishes theoretical foundation for characteristic function approach to pseudo-distributions and provides constructive experimental method for their direct measurement, connecting to fundamental quantum concepts like weak values and commutation relations.

title: Determining the ensemble N-representability of Reduced Density Matrices
summary: The N-representability problem for reduced density matrices remains a fundamental challenge in electronic structure theory. Following our previous work that employs a unitary-evolution algorithm based on an adaptive derivative-assembled pseudo-Trotter variational quantum algorithm to probe pure-state N-representability of reduced density matrices [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20, 9968], in this work we propose a practical framework for determining the ensemble N-representability of a p-body matrix. This is accomplished using a purification strategy consisting of embedding an ensemble state into a pure state defined on an extended Hilbert space, such that the reduced density matrices of the purified state reproduce those of the original ensemble. By iteratively applying variational unitaries to an initial purified state, the proposed algorithm minimizes the Hilbert-Schmidt distance between its p-body reduced density matrix and a specified target p-body matrix, which serves as a measure of the N-representability of the target. This methodology facilitates both error correction of defective ensemble reduced density matrices, and quantum-state reconstruction on a quantum computer, offering a route for density-matrix refinement. We validate the algorithm with numerical simulations on systems of two, three, and four electrons in both, simple models as well as molecular systems at finite temperature, demonstrating its robustness.

AI.tldr: A practical framework for determining ensemble N-representability of p-body matrices using purification strategy and variational quantum algorithms, enabling error correction and quantum-state reconstruction.
AI.motivation: The N-representability problem for reduced density matrices is a fundamental challenge in electronic structure theory. Previous work addressed pure-state N-representability, but ensemble N-representability remains an important open problem requiring practical solutions.
AI.method: Uses a purification strategy that embeds an ensemble state into a pure state on an extended Hilbert space. Applies variational unitaries to an initial purified state to minimize Hilbert-Schmidt distance between its p-body reduced density matrix and a target p-body matrix, serving as a measure of N-representability.
AI.result: Validated with numerical simulations on systems of two, three, and four electrons in both simple models and molecular systems at finite temperature, demonstrating robustness of the algorithm.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methodology facilitates error correction of defective ensemble reduced density matrices and quantum-state reconstruction on quantum computers, offering a route for density-matrix refinement and practical determination of ensemble N-representability.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo for Combinatorial Optimization
summary: Quantum computing offers an alternative paradigm for addressing combinatorial optimization problems compared to classical computing. Despite recent hardware improvements, the execution of empirical quantum optimization experiments at scales known to be hard for state-of-the-art classical solvers is not yet in reach. In this work, we offer a different way to approach combinatorial optimization with near-term quantum computing. Motivated by the promising results observed in using quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) for approximating complicated probability distributions, we combine ideas of sampling from the device with QeMCMC together with warm-starting and parallel tempering, in the context of combinatorial optimization. We demonstrate empirically that our algorithm recovers the global optima for instances of the Maximum Independent Set problem (MIS) up to 117 decision variables using 117 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. We show early evidence of a scaling advantage of our algorithm compared to similar classical methods for the chosen instances of MIS. MIS is practically relevant across domains like financial services and molecular biology, and, in some cases, already difficult to solve to optimality classically with only a few hundred decision variables.

AI.tldr: Quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm for combinatorial optimization achieves global optima for Maximum Independent Set problems up to 117 variables using 117 qubits on IBM hardware, showing early scaling advantage over classical methods.
AI.motivation: Quantum computing offers alternative approach to combinatorial optimization, but current hardware can't yet handle problem scales that challenge classical solvers. Need different approach for near-term quantum computing.
AI.method: Combines quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) with warm-starting and parallel tempering for combinatorial optimization. Uses quantum device sampling integrated with QeMCMC techniques.
AI.result: Algorithm recovers global optima for Maximum Independent Set instances up to 117 decision variables using 117 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. Shows early evidence of scaling advantage over similar classical methods.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates practical quantum approach for combinatorial optimization on near-term hardware, with relevance to domains like financial services and molecular biology where MIS problems are already classically challenging at modest scales.

title: Experimental Quantum Bernoulli Factories via Bell-Basis Measurements
summary: Randomness processing in the Bernoulli factory framework provides a concrete setting in which quantum resources can outperform classical ones. We experimentally demonstrate an entanglement-assisted quantum Bernoulli factory based on Bell-basis measurements of two identical input quoins prepared on IBM superconducting hardware. Using only the measurement outcomes (and no external classical randomness source), we realize the classically inconstructible Bernoulli doubling primitive $f(p)=2p$ and, as intermediate outputs from the same Bell-measurement statistics, an exact fair coin $f(p)=1/2$ and the classically inconstructible function $f(p)=4p(1-p)$. We benchmark the measured output biases against ideal predictions and discuss the impact of device noise. Our results establish a simple, resource-efficient experimental primitive for quantum-to-classical randomness processing and support the viability of quantum Bernoulli factories for quantum-enhanced stochastic simulation and sampling tasks.

AI.tldr: Experimental demonstration of entanglement-assisted quantum Bernoulli factory on IBM superconducting hardware, achieving classically impossible randomness processing functions like f(p)=2p without external classical randomness.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate quantum advantage in randomness processing through the Bernoulli factory framework, where quantum resources can outperform classical limitations, and to establish a resource-efficient experimental primitive for quantum-to-classical randomness processing.
AI.method: Implemented an entanglement-assisted quantum Bernoulli factory using Bell-basis measurements of two identical input quoins (quantum coins) prepared on IBM superconducting hardware. The approach uses only measurement outcomes without external classical randomness sources.
AI.result: Successfully realized three functions from the same Bell-measurement statistics: 1) the classically inconstructible Bernoulli doubling primitive f(p)=2p, 2) an exact fair coin f(p)=1/2, and 3) the classically inconstructible function f(p)=4p(1-p). Benchmarked output biases against ideal predictions and analyzed device noise impact.
AI.conclusion: The experiment establishes a simple, resource-efficient experimental primitive for quantum-to-classical randomness processing and supports the viability of quantum Bernoulli factories for quantum-enhanced stochastic simulation and sampling tasks.

title: Hybrid Quantum Image Preparation via JPEG Compression
summary: We present a hybrid classical-quantum image preparation scheme that reduces the quantum implementation cost of image loading for quantum pixel information encoding (QPIE). The proposed method, termed JPEG-assisted QPIE (JQPIE), loads only the quantized JPEG coefficients into a quantum register, leading to substantial reductions in \texttt{CX} gate count and circuit depth while preserving reconstruction quality comparable to classical JPEG compression. We develop two variants of the hybrid strategy. The first realizes the complete JPEG decompression pipeline coherently by implementing inverse quantization via a block-encoded unitary operator. The second, referred to as \emph{quantization-free JQPIE} (QF-JQPIE), omits quantization altogether, thereby avoiding the probabilistic nature of block-encoded quantization. Numerical simulations on standard benchmark image datasets (USC--SIPI and Kodak) demonstrate that both variants achieve significant constant-factor reductions in \texttt{CX} gate count and circuit depth relative to direct QPIE loading, while maintaining high reconstruction quality as measured by PSNR and SSIM.

AI.tldr: JQPIE reduces quantum image loading costs by leveraging JPEG compression, achieving significant CX gate and circuit depth reductions while maintaining reconstruction quality comparable to classical JPEG.
AI.motivation: Quantum image preparation using QPIE encoding has high implementation costs in terms of CX gate count and circuit depth. The authors aim to reduce these quantum resource requirements while preserving image quality.
AI.method: Two hybrid classical-quantum variants: 1) JQPIE loads quantized JPEG coefficients into quantum register and implements complete JPEG decompression pipeline coherently via block-encoded unitary operators for inverse quantization; 2) QF-JQPIE omits quantization entirely to avoid probabilistic nature of block-encoded quantization.
AI.result: Both variants achieve significant constant-factor reductions in CX gate count and circuit depth compared to direct QPIE loading, while maintaining high reconstruction quality (measured by PSNR and SSIM) on standard benchmark datasets (USC-SIPI and Kodak).
AI.conclusion: The hybrid classical-quantum approach successfully reduces quantum resource requirements for image loading while preserving reconstruction quality comparable to classical JPEG compression, making quantum image processing more practical.

title: Characterizing Quantum Error Correction Performance of Radiation-induced Errors
summary: Radiation impacts are a current challenge with computing on superconducting-based quantum devices because they can lead to widespread correlated errors across the device. Such errors can be problematic for quantum error correction (QEC) codes, which are generally designed to correct independent errors. To address this, we have developed a computational model to simulate the effects of radiation impacts on QEC performance. This is achieved by building from recently developed models of quasiparticle density, mapping radiation-induced qubit error rates onto a quantum error channel and simulation of a simple surface code. We also provide a performance metric to quantify the resilience of a QEC code to radiation impacts. Additionally, we sweep various parameters of chip design to test mitigation strategies for improved QEC performance. Our model approach is holistic, allowing for modular performance testing of error mitigation strategies and chip and code designs.

AI.tldr: Developed computational model to simulate radiation impact effects on quantum error correction performance, with performance metric and parameter sweeps for mitigation strategies.
AI.motivation: Radiation impacts cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum devices, which are problematic for QEC codes designed for independent errors.
AI.method: Built computational model from quasiparticle density models, mapped radiation-induced qubit error rates to quantum error channel, simulated simple surface code, and swept chip design parameters.
AI.result: Developed holistic model approach for modular performance testing of error mitigation strategies and chip/code designs with radiation resilience metric.
AI.conclusion: Provides framework to quantify and improve QEC resilience to radiation impacts through systematic modeling and parameter optimization.

title: Time-reversal Interferometry Using Cat States with Scalable Entangling Resources
summary: We propose a novel method for generating Schrödinger-cat states -- defined as equal superpositions of arbitrary coherent states -- using a concise sequence of rapid twist-and-turn pulses. We demonstrate that the required shearing strength for the protocol, which scales linearly with time, decreases with increasing number of atoms ($N$) in proportion to $1/\sqrt{N}$. The resulting states exhibit optimal quantum Fisher information, making them ideal for surpassing the classical limit of phase sensitivity in quantum metrology applications. Notably, our protocol is compatible with a time-reversal strategy for quantum metrology, ensuring its practical viability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Heisenberg limit scaling remains intact even when reducing the twisting employed in tandem with the number of atoms, thereby mitigating realistic losses such as photon scattering.

AI.tldr: Novel method generates Schrödinger-cat states using rapid twist-and-turn pulses with shearing strength scaling as 1/√N, achieving optimal quantum Fisher information for Heisenberg-limited quantum metrology while mitigating losses.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient method for generating Schrödinger-cat states (equal superpositions of arbitrary coherent states) that can surpass classical phase sensitivity limits in quantum metrology while addressing practical challenges like photon scattering losses.
AI.method: Uses a concise sequence of rapid twist-and-turn pulses to generate Schrödinger-cat states. The protocol requires shearing strength that scales linearly with time but decreases with atom number as 1/√N. The method is compatible with time-reversal strategies for quantum metrology.
AI.result: Successfully generates Schrödinger-cat states with optimal quantum Fisher information, enabling surpassing of classical phase sensitivity limits. The Heisenberg limit scaling is maintained even when reducing twisting in tandem with atom number, effectively mitigating realistic losses like photon scattering.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical and efficient approach to generate Schrödinger-cat states for quantum metrology applications, achieving Heisenberg-limited sensitivity while being robust against realistic experimental losses through optimized parameter scaling.

title: Lunar Silicon Cavity
summary: The Moon's permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) are among the coldest places in the Solar System and are expected to become key landing sites for upcoming international space agency missions. Their proximity to peaks of perpetual solar power and potential resource richness makes them prime candidates for lunar exploration and future Moon bases. Here we propose to deploy a passive, ultrastable optical resonator in these regions that will enable laser systems with unprecedented phase-coherence. The unique physical environment of lunar PSRs greatly benefits the construction of a cryogenic monolithic silicon cavity that exhibits low $10^{-18}$ thermal noise-limited stability and coherence time exceeding 1 minute, more than a decade better than the current best terrestrial system. Such a stable laser will form a basic quantum technology infrastructure in space to serve many applications, including establishing a lunar time standard, building long-baseline optical interferometry, distribution of stable optical signals across networks of satellites, testing general relativity and gravitational physics, and forming the backbone for space-based quantum networks.

AI.tldr: Proposal to deploy ultrastable optical resonators in lunar permanently shadowed regions to achieve unprecedented laser coherence for space-based quantum technologies.
AI.motivation: Lunar PSRs offer unique cryogenic conditions ideal for building ultrastable optical cavities, enabling laser systems with phase-coherence far beyond terrestrial capabilities for space-based applications.
AI.method: Deploy passive ultrastable optical resonators in lunar permanently shadowed regions to construct cryogenic monolithic silicon cavities that leverage the extreme cold environment for thermal noise reduction.
AI.result: Achieves low 10^-18 thermal noise-limited stability and coherence time exceeding 1 minute, representing more than a decade improvement over current best terrestrial systems.
AI.conclusion: Such ultrastable lasers would establish fundamental quantum technology infrastructure in space for applications including lunar time standards, optical interferometry, satellite networks, gravitational physics tests, and space-based quantum networks.

title: Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Resistant to General Attacks
summary: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) produce true random numbers based on the inherent randomness of quantum theory, rendering them a foundational segment of quantum cryptography. Distinguished from trusted-device QRNGs whose security depends on characterized devices, semi-device-independent (semi-DI) QRNGs permit partial devices to be defective or even maliciously manipulated, which achieves a good trade-off between generation rate and security. In this paper, we propose a semi-DI QRNG that resists general attacks while accounting for finite-size effects. The protocol requires no rigorous characterization of the source and measurement devices other than limiting the energy of the emitted states, significantly reducing the demands on practical QRNG systems. Leveraging the tight Kato inequality for correlated variables, we show that our protocol generates more randomness than it consumes. Furthermore, we demonstrate the scheme on a continuous-variable system with ternary inputs of states. Heterodyne detection is employed to enable phase compensation through data postprocessing, alleviating the stringent requirement on system stability. The system operates at 100 MHz, achieving a net random number generation rate of 1.165 Mbps at 5.3x10^9 rounds. Our work offers a promising approach to achieve both the robust security and high generation rate with a simple experimental setup.

AI.tldr: A semi-device-independent quantum random number generator that resists general attacks while accounting for finite-size effects, achieving 1.165 Mbps net generation rate with simple experimental setup.
AI.motivation: To develop a QRNG that balances security and generation rate by reducing device characterization requirements while maintaining robustness against general attacks, addressing the limitations of trusted-device QRNGs.
AI.method: Semi-device-independent protocol requiring only energy limitation of emitted states, using tight Kato inequality for correlated variables, implemented on continuous-variable system with ternary inputs and heterodyne detection with phase compensation via postprocessing.
AI.result: System operates at 100 MHz, achieves net random number generation rate of 1.165 Mbps at 5.3×10^9 rounds, demonstrating more randomness generation than consumption.
AI.conclusion: The proposed semi-DI QRNG offers robust security and high generation rate with simple experimental setup, representing a promising approach for practical quantum random number generation.

title: Quenching Speculation in Quantum Markets via Entangled Neural Traders
summary: Speculative trading can drive pronounced market instabilities, yet existing regulatory and macroprudential tools intervene only after such dynamics emerge. Quantum technologies offer a fundamentally new means of shaping economic behavior by introducing non-classical correlations between decision-makers. Here we demonstrate a prototype quantum stock market in which entanglement between traders' valuations mitigates the runaway devaluation characteristic of speculative busts. Using reinforcement-learning agents trading a single commodity, we show that replacing classical valuations with quantum-correlated qubit-encoded valuations stabilizes prices and increases the AI traders' net worth relative to a classical market, where instead agents rapidly converge to liquidation strategies that collapse the asset value. To explain this behavior, we formulate and analyze a quantized version of the $p$-guessing game, a canonical model of speculative dynamics. Quantum entanglement and phase coherence reshape the strategic landscape, eliminating the pathological pure-strategy Nash equilibrium that drives market collapse in the classical game, while mixed-strategy equilibria remain non-degenerate and avoid bust-type outcomes. These results identify quantum correlations as a novel, endogenous mechanism for market stabilization and, more broadly, demonstrate the utility of multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms for uncovering optimal strategies in complex decision-making frameworks with quantum degrees of freedom.

AI.tldr: Quantum entanglement between traders' valuations stabilizes speculative markets by eliminating pathological Nash equilibria that cause price collapses in classical markets.
AI.motivation: Existing regulatory tools intervene only after speculative instabilities emerge; quantum technologies offer a fundamentally new means of shaping economic behavior through non-classical correlations between decision-makers.
AI.method: Created a prototype quantum stock market with reinforcement-learning agents trading a single commodity, replacing classical valuations with quantum-correlated qubit-encoded valuations. Also formulated and analyzed a quantized version of the p-guessing game to explain the behavior.
AI.result: Quantum entanglement stabilizes prices and increases AI traders' net worth relative to classical markets, where agents rapidly converge to liquidation strategies that collapse asset value. Quantum correlations reshape the strategic landscape, eliminating pathological pure-strategy Nash equilibria that drive market collapse.
AI.conclusion: Quantum correlations serve as a novel, endogenous mechanism for market stabilization, demonstrating the utility of multi-agent reinforcement learning for uncovering optimal strategies in complex decision-making frameworks with quantum degrees of freedom.

title: HyQuRP: Hybrid quantum-classical neural network with rotational and permutational equivariance for 3D point clouds
summary: We introduce HyQuRP, a hybrid quantum-classical neural network equivariant to rotational and permutational symmetries. While existing equivariant quantum machine learning models often rely on ad hoc constructions, HyQuRP is built upon the formal foundations of group representation theory. In the sparse-point regime, HyQuRP consistently outperforms strong classical and quantum baselines across multiple benchmarks. For example, when six subsampled points are used, HyQuRP ($\sim$1.5K parameters) achieves 76.13% accuracy on the 5-class ModelNet benchmark, compared to approximately 71% for PointNet, PointMamba, and PointTransformer with similar parameter counts. These results highlight HyQuRP's exceptional data efficiency and suggest the potential of quantum machine learning models for processing 3D point cloud data.

AI.tldr: HyQuRP is a hybrid quantum-classical neural network with rotational and permutational symmetry equivariance that outperforms classical and quantum baselines in sparse-point 3D point cloud classification.
AI.motivation: Existing equivariant quantum machine learning models often use ad hoc constructions rather than formal mathematical foundations. The authors aim to develop a principled quantum-classical model with proper symmetry equivariance for 3D point cloud data processing.
AI.method: HyQuRP is built using group representation theory to ensure rotational and permutational symmetry equivariance. It combines quantum and classical neural network components in a hybrid architecture specifically designed for sparse-point regimes in 3D point cloud data.
AI.result: HyQuRP consistently outperforms strong classical and quantum baselines across multiple benchmarks. With only six subsampled points, HyQuRP (∼1.5K parameters) achieves 76.13% accuracy on the 5-class ModelNet benchmark, compared to approximately 71% for PointNet, PointMamba, and PointTransformer with similar parameter counts.
AI.conclusion: HyQuRP demonstrates exceptional data efficiency and suggests the potential of quantum machine learning models for processing 3D point cloud data, particularly in sparse-point regimes where it outperforms established classical methods.

title: Achieving Sub-Exponential Speedup in Gate-Based Quantum Computing for Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization
summary:
Recent quantum-inspired methods based on the Simulated Annealing algorithm have shown strong potential for solving combinatorial optimization problems. However, Grover's algorithm in gate-based quantum computing offers only a quadratic speedup, which remains impractical for large problem sizes. This paper proposes a hybrid approach that integrates Simulated Annealing with Grover's algorithm to achieve sub-exponential speedup, thereby improving its industrial applicability.
  In enzyme fermentation, variables such as temperature, stirring, wait time, pH, tryptophan, rice flour and others are encoded by 625 binary parameters, defining the space of possible enzyme formulations. We aim to find a binary configuration that maximizes the active ingredient, formulated as a 625-bit Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization problem generated from historical experiments and artificial intelligence techniques. Minimizing the QUBO cost corresponds to maximizing the active ingredient. This case study demonstrates that the proposed hybrid method achieves sub-exponential speedup using gate-based quantum computing.

AI.tldr: Hybrid approach combining Simulated Annealing with Grover's algorithm achieves sub-exponential speedup for solving 625-bit QUBO problems in enzyme fermentation optimization.
AI.motivation: Quantum-inspired methods show promise for combinatorial optimization, but Grover's algorithm alone offers only quadratic speedup, which is insufficient for practical industrial applications with large problem sizes.
AI.method: Proposes a hybrid approach integrating Simulated Annealing with Grover's algorithm. Encodes enzyme fermentation variables (temperature, stirring, wait time, pH, tryptophan, rice flour, etc.) into 625 binary parameters, formulating the optimization as a 625-bit Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization problem derived from historical experiments and AI techniques.
AI.result: The hybrid method achieves sub-exponential speedup (beyond quadratic) for solving the 625-bit QUBO problem using gate-based quantum computing, demonstrating improved industrial applicability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Simulated Annealing-Grover hybrid approach provides practical sub-exponential speedup for combinatorial optimization problems, making quantum computing more viable for industrial applications like enzyme fermentation optimization.

title: Coherent Spin-Photon Interface of single PL6 Color Centers in Silicon Carbide
summary: The PL6 color center in silicon carbide has recently emerged as a promising platform for quantum information processing, yet its coherent spin--photon interface has remained largely unexplored. Here we present a comprehensive investigation of single PL6 centers, combining spectroscopy with theoretical analysis. The excited-state fine structure is fully resolved using group-theoretical modeling and strain-dependent measurements. Under resonant excitation, we achieve a spin initialization fidelity of $99.69 \pm 0.03\%$ and a readout contrast of $98.31 \pm 1.03\%$. The spin--photon--entangled $A_2$ transition exhibits narrow optical linewidths ($\sim 180$~MHz) and a polarization visibility of $\sim 82\%$. Coherent optical driving enables Rabi frequencies up to $2.895$~GHz, while dynamical decoupling extends the spin coherence time from $0.5$~ms to $5.70$~ms. Our results establish PL6 as a competitive solid-state spin--photon interface hosted in a commercially available semiconductor platform.

AI.tldr: PL6 color centers in silicon carbide demonstrate high-performance spin-photon interface with excellent spin initialization/readout fidelities, narrow optical linewidths, and extended coherence times through dynamical decoupling.
AI.motivation: PL6 color centers in silicon carbide show promise for quantum information processing, but their coherent spin-photon interface remains largely unexplored, requiring comprehensive investigation to establish their competitiveness as solid-state quantum platforms.
AI.method: Combined spectroscopy with theoretical analysis using group-theoretical modeling and strain-dependent measurements to resolve excited-state fine structure, resonant excitation for spin manipulation, and dynamical decoupling techniques to extend coherence times.
AI.result: Achieved spin initialization fidelity of 99.69±0.03%, readout contrast of 98.31±1.03%, narrow optical linewidths (~180 MHz) with 82% polarization visibility, Rabi frequencies up to 2.895 GHz, and extended spin coherence time from 0.5 ms to 5.70 ms using dynamical decoupling.
AI.conclusion: PL6 color centers establish themselves as competitive solid-state spin-photon interfaces hosted in commercially available silicon carbide, offering high-performance quantum information processing capabilities.

title: Quantum Dynamics of Vibrationally-Assisted Electron Transfer beyond Condon approximation in the Ligand-Receptor Complex
summary: We investigate the quantum dynamics of ligand--receptor electron transfer and conformational response in a prototypical viral binding complex, using the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein bound to the human ACE2 receptor as a model system. Treating the ACE2--Spike interface as an open quantum system embedded in a biological environment, we simulate how vibrational interactions and environmental memory reshape the coupled receptor--ligand dynamics and modulate vibrationally assisted electron transfer (VA-ET). Using a Non-Markovian Stochastic Schr"odinger Equation (NMSSE) approach, we simulate electron transfer between donor and acceptor states in ACE2 modulated by a specific vibrational mode of the Spike protein. The influence of environmental memory (non-Markovian dynamics) and non-Condon effects (vibrational modulation of electronic coupling) are analyzed in detail. In the Markovian limit with an Ohmic bath, population dynamics reduce to exponential kinetics, and extracted transfer rates agree with semiclassical Marcus--Jortner predictions in the appropriate regime. Beyond the Markovian, high-temperature limit, we observe clear deviations: non-exponential decay, coherent oscillatory features, and enhanced sensitivity to the vibrational frequency. Incorporating off-diagonal system--bath coupling alongside diagonal coupling shows that nuclear motion can dynamically gate electron tunneling, sharpening the frequency selectivity of the VA-ET mechanism. Finally, a structured (sub-Ohmic) environmental spectral density with long-lived correlations (``memory'') preserves electronic--vibrational coherence over longer times, amplifying vibrational selectivity under non-Condon coupling. Our results support the proposition that ACE2--Spike binding may exploit vibrational assistance and quantum coherence as a molecular recognition mechanism.

AI.tldr: Quantum dynamics study of SARS-CoV-2 Spike-ACE2 binding reveals vibrationally assisted electron transfer with non-Markovian environmental memory effects that enhance vibrational selectivity and coherence.
AI.motivation: Investigate quantum dynamics of ligand-receptor electron transfer and conformational response in viral binding complexes, using SARS-CoV-2 Spike-ACE2 as a model system to understand how vibrational interactions and environmental memory reshape coupled receptor-ligand dynamics.
AI.method: Treat ACE2-Spike interface as open quantum system in biological environment; simulate vibrationally assisted electron transfer using Non-Markovian Stochastic Schrödinger Equation (NMSSE) approach; analyze electron transfer between donor/acceptor states modulated by specific Spike vibrational mode; examine environmental memory (non-Markovian dynamics) and non-Condon effects (vibrational modulation of electronic coupling).
AI.result: Markovian limit with Ohmic bath yields exponential kinetics matching semiclassical Marcus-Jortner predictions; beyond Markovian/high-temperature limit shows non-exponential decay, coherent oscillations, enhanced vibrational frequency sensitivity; nuclear motion dynamically gates electron tunneling, sharpening frequency selectivity; structured (sub-Ohmic) spectral density with long-lived correlations preserves electronic-vibrational coherence longer, amplifying vibrational selectivity under non-Condon coupling.
AI.conclusion: ACE2-Spike binding may exploit vibrational assistance and quantum coherence as molecular recognition mechanism, with environmental memory effects playing crucial role in modulating electron transfer dynamics and enhancing vibrational selectivity.

title: Local Certification of Many-Body Steady States
summary: We present a relaxation-based method to bound expectation values on the steady state of dissipative many-body quantum systems described by master equations of the Lindblad form. Instead of targeting to represent the entire state, we promote the reduced density matrices to our variables and enforce the constraints that are imposed on them by consistency with a global steady state. The resulting constraints have the form of a semidefinite program, which allows us to efficiently bound the values a given expectation value can take in the steady state. Our results show fast convergence of the bounds with the size of the reduced density matrices, giving very competitive predictions for the steady state of several one- and two-dimensional models for an arbitrary number of particles.

AI.tldr: A relaxation-based method using semidefinite programming to bound expectation values on steady states of dissipative many-body quantum systems by enforcing constraints on reduced density matrices.
AI.motivation: To efficiently compute bounds on expectation values for steady states of dissipative many-body quantum systems without needing to represent the entire quantum state, which is computationally expensive for large systems.
AI.method: Promotes reduced density matrices to variables and enforces constraints imposed by consistency with a global steady state. Formulates these constraints as a semidefinite program to efficiently bound expectation values.
AI.result: Shows fast convergence of bounds with the size of reduced density matrices, providing competitive predictions for steady states of various one- and two-dimensional models for arbitrary numbers of particles.
AI.conclusion: The relaxation-based semidefinite programming approach offers an efficient method to bound expectation values in dissipative many-body quantum systems, avoiding the computational complexity of full state representation while maintaining accuracy.

title: Algebraic Reduction to Improve an Optimally Bounded Quantum State Preparation Algorithm
summary: The preparation of $n$-qubit quantum states is a cross-cutting subroutine for many quantum algorithms, and the effort to reduce its circuit complexity is a significant challenge. In the literature, the quantum state preparation algorithm by Sun et al. is known to be optimally bounded, defining the asymptotically optimal width-depth trade-off bounds with and without ancillary qubits. In this work, a simpler algebraic decomposition is proposed to separate the preparation of the real part of the desired state from the complex one, resulting in a reduction in terms of circuit depth, total gates, and CNOT count when $m$ ancillary qubits are available. The reduction in complexity is due to the use of a single operator $Λ$ for each uniformly controlled gate, instead of the three in the original decomposition. Using the PennyLane library, this new algorithm for state preparation has been implemented and tested in a simulated environment for both dense and sparse quantum states, including those that are random and of physical interest. Furthermore, its performance has been compared with that of Möttönen et al.'s algorithm, which is a de facto standard for preparing quantum states in cases where no ancillary qubits are used, highlighting interesting lines of development.

AI.tldr: A new quantum state preparation algorithm reduces circuit complexity by separating real and complex parts, using fewer operators per uniformly controlled gate, achieving better depth, gate count, and CNOT efficiency with ancillary qubits.
AI.motivation: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for many quantum algorithms, and reducing its circuit complexity is crucial for practical quantum computing. While Sun et al.'s algorithm is known to be optimally bounded, there's room for improvement in practical implementations, especially when ancillary qubits are available.
AI.method: The proposed method uses a simpler algebraic decomposition that separates the preparation of the real part from the complex part of the desired quantum state. This approach uses a single operator Λ for each uniformly controlled gate instead of the three operators required in the original decomposition, leading to reduced circuit complexity.
AI.result: The new algorithm achieves reductions in circuit depth, total gate count, and CNOT count when m ancillary qubits are available. It was implemented and tested using the PennyLane library for both dense and sparse quantum states, including random states and physically interesting states. Performance comparisons with Möttönen et al.'s algorithm (the standard for no-ancilla cases) revealed interesting development opportunities.
AI.conclusion: The proposed algebraic decomposition provides a more efficient quantum state preparation algorithm that reduces circuit complexity metrics while maintaining functionality. The separation of real and complex parts and the use of single operators per uniformly controlled gate offer practical advantages, especially when ancillary qubits are available, suggesting promising directions for further development in quantum state preparation techniques.

title: Extensible universal photonic quantum computing with nonlinearity
summary: Universal quantum computing requires an architecture that supports both linear circuits and, crucially, strong nonlinear resources. For quantum photonic systems, integrating such nonlinearities with scalable linear circuitry has been a major bottleneck, leaving most optical experiments without nonlinear operations and, consequently, incapable of achieving universality. Here, we report an extensible photonic computer that supports a universal gate set by seamlessly combining fully programmable, scalable linear optical networks with integrated nonlinear modules. This platform enables a broad range of quantum computing and simulation tasks. We demonstrate the quasi-deterministic generation of optical Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, which are essential resources for bosonic error correction, yet had previously been realized only probabilistically. Furthermore, we simulate complex many-body quantum dynamics, exemplified by the Bose-Hubbard model. Such quantum simulation tasks have long been considered beyond the reach of photonic hardware limited to linear operations. These capabilities, enabled by our extensible architecture, establish a viable route towards photonic quantum simulation and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

AI.tldr: Extensible photonic computer combining programmable linear optical networks with integrated nonlinear modules enables universal quantum computing, demonstrated through quasi-deterministic GKP state generation and Bose-Hubbard model simulation.
AI.motivation: Universal quantum computing requires both linear circuits and strong nonlinear resources, but photonic systems have struggled to integrate nonlinearities with scalable linear circuitry, leaving most optical experiments incapable of achieving universality.
AI.method: Developed an extensible photonic computer architecture that seamlessly combines fully programmable, scalable linear optical networks with integrated nonlinear modules to support a universal gate set.
AI.result: Demonstrated quasi-deterministic generation of optical Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states (previously only realized probabilistically) and simulation of complex many-body quantum dynamics via the Bose-Hubbard model.
AI.conclusion: The extensible architecture establishes a viable route towards photonic quantum simulation and fault-tolerant quantum computing by overcoming the bottleneck of integrating nonlinearities with scalable linear circuitry.

title: High-speed phase-encoded quantum secure direct communication over 11.4 km heterogeneous free-space and fiber links
summary: Robust quantum transmission is driving a new paradigm in space-ground quantum networking. Although phase encoding has been widely adopted in terrestrial fiber channels, it has long been considered unsuitable for free-space quantum communication. Here, we demonstrate phase-encoded quantum communication over 1400 m of urban free space. The system maintained stable operation for nearly one hour, achieving 99.07% interference visibility and an average quantum bit error rate of 2.38%. The free-space quantum states were directly coupled into the fiber and transmitted over an additional 10 km, confirming seamless interoperability across different media. We further show that turbulence-induced phase drifts between successive picosecond pulses can be effectively compensated. A cascaded-link model and numerical simulations indicate feasibility over free-space distances exceeding 30 km, underscoring the potential for satellite-to-ground quantum links. This work establishes the viability of phase encoding in free-space quantum networks, simplifying cross-medium integration and enabling compatibility with existing classical infrastructures.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of phase-encoded quantum communication over 1400m urban free space with 99.07% interference visibility and 2.38% QBER, showing feasibility for satellite-ground links up to 30km.
AI.motivation: Phase encoding has been widely used in terrestrial fiber quantum communication but was considered unsuitable for free-space quantum communication due to atmospheric turbulence and phase instability. The paper aims to demonstrate that phase encoding can work in free-space environments, enabling seamless integration between fiber and free-space quantum networks and compatibility with existing classical infrastructure.
AI.method: The researchers implemented a phase-encoded quantum communication system over 1400m of urban free space. They developed techniques to compensate for turbulence-induced phase drifts between successive picosecond pulses. The free-space quantum states were directly coupled into fiber and transmitted over an additional 10km. They used a cascaded-link model and numerical simulations to analyze system performance and scalability.
AI.result: The system maintained stable operation for nearly one hour with 99.07% interference visibility and average quantum bit error rate of 2.38%. Successful direct coupling of free-space quantum states into fiber with 10km additional transmission demonstrated seamless interoperability. The cascaded-link model and simulations indicate feasibility over free-space distances exceeding 30km, supporting potential for satellite-to-ground quantum links.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the viability of phase encoding in free-space quantum networks, simplifying cross-medium integration and enabling compatibility with existing classical infrastructures. The demonstration of turbulence compensation and long-distance feasibility (30km+) supports the potential for satellite-to-ground quantum communication links using phase encoding.

title: Normal mode splitting induced synchronization blockade in coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in Physical Review A as a letter
summary: We report a normal-mode induced synchronization blockade in coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators under the influence of external drive. In this mechanism, the coupling hybridizes the oscillator modes into spectrally split normal modes. The destructive interference between the transitions to these modes blocks synchronization. We find that this blockade can be controlled simply by tuning the coupling strength and detuning allowing dynamic manipulation of quantum synchronization through collective mode dynamics. We analyze the phase-locking behaviour using perturbation analysis. Further, by deriving steady-state probability amplitudes we show how the energy redistribution and spectral splitting forms the basis of the blockade. Our results might provide new insights into how synchronization can be controlled in quantum systems.

AI.tldr: Normal-mode induced synchronization blockade in coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators driven externally, controlled by coupling strength and detuning via destructive interference between transitions to spectrally split normal modes.
AI.motivation: To understand and control synchronization in quantum systems, particularly exploring how coupling and external drive affect synchronization blockade in quantum oscillators.
AI.method: Analysis of coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators under external drive using perturbation analysis to study phase-locking behavior, derivation of steady-state probability amplitudes to examine energy redistribution and spectral splitting.
AI.result: Discovery of normal-mode induced synchronization blockade mechanism where coupling hybridizes oscillator modes into spectrally split normal modes, with destructive interference between transitions to these modes blocking synchronization, controllable via coupling strength and detuning.
AI.conclusion: The normal-mode induced synchronization blockade provides a mechanism for dynamic manipulation of quantum synchronization through collective mode dynamics, offering new insights into controlling synchronization in quantum systems.

title: A Complete Equational Theory for Real-Clifford+CH Quantum Circuits
summary: We introduce a complete equational theory for the fragment of quantum circuits generated by the real Clifford gates plus the two-qubit controlled-Hadamard gate. That is, we give a simple set of equalities between circuits of this fragment, and prove that any other true equation can be derived from these. This is the first such completeness result for a finitely-generated, universal fragment of quantum circuits, with no parameterized gates and no need for ancillas.

AI.tldr: First completeness proof for real Clifford + controlled-Hadamard quantum circuits without ancillas or parameterized gates.
AI.motivation: To establish a complete equational theory for a universal, finitely-generated quantum circuit fragment without requiring ancillas or parameterized gates, addressing a gap in formal verification and circuit optimization.
AI.method: Developed a set of simple equalities between circuits using real Clifford gates and controlled-Hadamard gate, then proved completeness by showing any true equation can be derived from these axioms.
AI.result: Achieved the first completeness result for a finitely-generated, universal quantum circuit fragment without ancillas or parameterized gates, providing a complete equational theory for real Clifford + controlled-Hadamard circuits.
AI.conclusion: Established a foundational completeness theorem for quantum circuit verification and optimization, enabling formal reasoning about circuits in this universal fragment without additional resources.

title: Quantum Attention by Overlap Interference: Predicting Sequences from Classical and Many-Body Quantum Data
summary: We propose a variational quantum implementation of self-attention (QSA), the core operation in transformers and large language models, which predicts future elements of a sequence by forming overlap-weighted combinations of past data. At variance with previous approaches, our QSA realizes the required nonlinearity through interference of state overlaps and returns a Renyi-1/2 cross-entropy loss directly as the expectation value of an observable, avoiding the need to decode amplitude-encoded predictions into classical logits. Furthermore, QSA naturally accommodates a constrained, trainable data-embedding that ties quantum state overlaps to data-level similarities. We find a gate complexity dominant scaling O(T d^2) for QSA, versus O(T^2 d) classically, suggesting an advantage in the practical regime where the sequence length T dominates the embedding size d. In simulations, we show that our QSA-based quantum transformer learns sequence prediction on classical data and on many-body transverse-field Ising quantum trajectories, establishing trainable attention as a practical primitive for quantum dynamical modeling.

AI.tldr: Variational quantum self-attention (QSA) implementation using quantum interference for nonlinearity and Renyi-1/2 cross-entropy loss as observable expectation, with potential quantum advantage for long sequences.
AI.motivation: To develop a quantum implementation of self-attention (core transformer operation) that leverages quantum advantages, avoids classical decoding overhead, and enables practical quantum dynamical modeling.
AI.method: QSA uses quantum interference for nonlinearity, encodes data with trainable embeddings tied to quantum state overlaps, and computes Renyi-1/2 cross-entropy loss directly as observable expectation values without amplitude decoding.
AI.result: Gate complexity scales as O(T d^2) vs classical O(T^2 d), suggesting quantum advantage when sequence length T dominates embedding size d. Simulations show successful learning on classical data and quantum many-body Ising trajectories.
AI.conclusion: QSA establishes trainable attention as a practical primitive for quantum dynamical modeling, demonstrating quantum advantage potential and effective learning on both classical and quantum data.

title: Geometry of restricted information: the case of quantum thermodynamics
summary: We formulate a geometric framework in which physical laws emerge from restricted access to microscopic information. Measurement constraints are modeled as a gauge symmetry acting on density operators, inducing a gauge-reduced space of physically distinguishable states. In the case of quantum thermodynamics, this construction leads to a gauge-invariant formulation in which the invariant entropy admits a stochastic description and satisfies a general detailed fluctuation theorem. From this result, we derive an integrated fluctuation theorem and a Clausius-like inequality that unifies the first and second laws in terms of invariant work and coherent heat. Entropy production is identified with the relative entropy between forward and backward probability measures on the gauge-reduced space of thermodynamic trajectories, revealing irreversibility as a geometric consequence of limited observability. The third law emerges as a singular zero-temperature limit in which thermodynamic orbits collapse and entropy production vanishes. Since the framework applies to arbitrary information constraints, it encompasses energy-based thermodynamics as a particular case of more general measurement scenarios.

AI.tldr: Geometric framework where physical laws emerge from restricted access to microscopic information via gauge symmetry, leading to gauge-invariant thermodynamics with fluctuation theorems and unified laws.
AI.motivation: To develop a fundamental framework where physical laws emerge from measurement constraints and limited observability, rather than being fundamental, with particular application to quantum thermodynamics.
AI.method: Model measurement constraints as gauge symmetry acting on density operators, creating gauge-reduced space of physically distinguishable states; apply to quantum thermodynamics to derive gauge-invariant formulation with invariant entropy and fluctuation theorems.
AI.result: Derived detailed fluctuation theorem for invariant entropy, integrated fluctuation theorem, Clausius-like inequality unifying first and second laws, identification of entropy production as relative entropy between forward/backward measures, and emergence of third law as singular zero-temperature limit.
AI.conclusion: Physical laws emerge from information constraints; irreversibility is geometric consequence of limited observability; framework generalizes energy-based thermodynamics to arbitrary measurement scenarios.

title: Bridging Quantum and Semi-Classical Thermodynamics in Cavity QED
summary: In cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED), photons leaving the cavity can be irreversibly lost or reused as a power source. This dichotomy is reflected in two different thermodynamic bookkeepings of the light field, both corresponding to valid thermodynamic frameworks. In this work, we formulate a rigorous semi-classical limit of cavity QED and show that the resulting thermodynamic description may qualitatively differ from that of the fully quantised model. We find that violations of the thermodynamic uncertainty relations are recovered in the semi-classical limit only by one of the two thermodynamic frameworks: the one which treats part of the photon flux as a power source. We illustrate our findings in a three-level system coupled to a driven cavity.

AI.tldr: Semi-classical limit of cavity QED reveals thermodynamic framework dependence: only the framework treating photon flux as power source recovers thermodynamic uncertainty relations in the semi-classical limit.
AI.motivation: To resolve the thermodynamic dichotomy in cavity QED where photons can be either irreversibly lost or reused as power source, and to understand how the semi-classical limit affects thermodynamic descriptions compared to fully quantized models.
AI.method: Formulate a rigorous semi-classical limit of cavity QED and analyze thermodynamic frameworks, applying the approach to a three-level system coupled to a driven cavity.
AI.result: The semi-classical thermodynamic description qualitatively differs from the fully quantized model. Violations of thermodynamic uncertainty relations are recovered in the semi-classical limit only by the framework treating part of the photon flux as a power source.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic framework choice in cavity QED significantly impacts the semi-classical limit behavior, with only the power-source framework maintaining consistency with thermodynamic uncertainty relations.

title: Heralding efficiency and brightness optimization of a micro-ring resonator via tunable coupling
summary: Efficient and bright single photon sources on photonic chips are key to scaling quantum technologies. Spontaneous four wave mixing in micro-ring resonators creates excellent narrowband and tunable photon sources. We experimentally demonstrate the optimization of heralding efficiency and brightness by tuning the coupling of the pump, signal and idler modes into the resonator whilst operating in a pulsed pump regime. We observe a maximum detected pair rate of over 93,000~coincidences per second in a moderately over-coupled regime, alongside a high intrinsic idler heralding efficiency of 97.87$\pm$8.97\% when operating close to maximal over-coupling. The measured dependence on coupling strength is in strong agreement with theoretical predictions, experimentally validating the predicted trade-off between brightness and heralding efficiency.

AI.tldr: Experimental optimization of micro-ring resonator photon sources achieves 93,000 coincidences/second with 97.87% intrinsic idler heralding efficiency by tuning mode coupling in pulsed regime.
AI.motivation: Efficient and bright single photon sources on photonic chips are essential for scaling quantum technologies, requiring optimization of both brightness and heralding efficiency.
AI.method: Experimental demonstration using spontaneous four-wave mixing in micro-ring resonators with pulsed pump regime, tuning coupling of pump, signal, and idler modes into the resonator.
AI.result: Maximum detected pair rate of over 93,000 coincidences per second in moderately over-coupled regime, with intrinsic idler heralding efficiency of 97.87±8.97% near maximal over-coupling.
AI.conclusion: Experimental validation of theoretical trade-off between brightness and heralding efficiency, demonstrating optimal performance through controlled coupling strength tuning.

title: Phase-sensitive characterization of a quantum frequency converter by spectral interferometry
summary: We introduce an experimental technique for complete phase-sensitive characterization of arbitrary unitary spectral-temporal transformations of optical modes. Our method recovers the complex spectral transfer function, or Green's function, of a frequency converter by analyzing spectral interference in the response to a tunable bichromatic probe. We perform a proof-of-concept experiment on a frequency conversion module based on Bragg-scattering four-wave mixing in photonic crystal fiber. Our results validate our technique by recovering useful information in the phase of the Green's function, revealing the relative positions of regions of active frequency conversion and passive dispersive propagation within the module. Our work introduces a new approach to characterizing the performance of a variety of active devices with diverse applications in emerging quantum technologies.

AI.tldr: Experimental technique for complete phase-sensitive characterization of arbitrary unitary spectral-temporal transformations of optical modes by recovering complex spectral transfer function through spectral interference analysis of tunable bichromatic probe responses.
AI.motivation: Need for complete phase-sensitive characterization of arbitrary unitary spectral-temporal transformations of optical modes, particularly for active devices in emerging quantum technologies where phase information is crucial.
AI.method: Analyzes spectral interference in response to tunable bichromatic probe to recover complex spectral transfer function (Green's function). Experimental validation performed on frequency conversion module based on Bragg-scattering four-wave mixing in photonic crystal fiber.
AI.result: Successfully recovered useful phase information in Green's function, revealing relative positions of regions of active frequency conversion and passive dispersive propagation within the module, validating the technique.
AI.conclusion: Introduces new approach for characterizing performance of various active devices with applications in emerging quantum technologies, enabling complete phase-sensitive characterization of spectral-temporal transformations.

title: Hybrid Coupling Topology with Dynamic ZZ Suppression for Optimizing Circuit Depth during Runtime in Superconducting Quantum Processor
summary: To reduce circuit depth when executing Quantum algorithms, it is necessary to maximize qubit connectivity on a near-term quantum processor. While addressing this, we also need to ensure high gate fidelity, suppression of unwanted ZZ cross-talk, a compact layout footprint, and minimal control hardware complexity to support scalability. In current superconducting quantum chips, fixed coupling is used as it is easier to scale, but it is limited by unwanted static ZZ interaction during single qubit operations, which degrades system performance. To overcome these challenges, we have introduced a first-of-its-kind hybrid tunable-coupling architecture that connects four fixed-frequency transmon qubits using a single coupler. This hybrid coupler uses off-resonant Stark drives to tune ZZ strength between qubit pairs. Experimentally backed simulation results indicate that our proposed hybrid design maximizes the qubit connectivity while reducing control overhead. This design achieves a near 20% reduction in circuit depth compared to IBM's Heavy-Hexagonal layout, showing its potential for scalability.

AI.tldr: A hybrid tunable-coupling architecture for superconducting quantum processors that connects four fixed-frequency transmon qubits via a single coupler, using off-resonant Stark drives to tune ZZ strength, achieving 20% circuit depth reduction compared to IBM's Heavy-Hexagonal layout.
AI.motivation: To reduce circuit depth in quantum algorithms by maximizing qubit connectivity while maintaining high gate fidelity, suppressing unwanted ZZ cross-talk, minimizing layout footprint, and reducing control hardware complexity for scalability. Current fixed-coupling architectures suffer from static ZZ interactions that degrade performance during single-qubit operations.
AI.method: Introduces a first-of-its-kind hybrid tunable-coupling architecture connecting four fixed-frequency transmon qubits using a single coupler. The hybrid coupler employs off-resonant Stark drives to dynamically tune ZZ interaction strength between qubit pairs, enabling flexible connectivity while maintaining control simplicity.
AI.result: Experimentally backed simulations show the design maximizes qubit connectivity while reducing control overhead. Achieves approximately 20% reduction in circuit depth compared to IBM's Heavy-Hexagonal layout, demonstrating potential for scalability in near-term quantum processors.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid tunable-coupling architecture successfully addresses key challenges in superconducting quantum processors by balancing connectivity, fidelity, and scalability, offering a promising approach for reducing circuit depth in quantum algorithm execution on near-term hardware.

title: Comment on "Relativistic covariance and nonlinear quantum mechanics: Tomonaga-Schwinger analysis''
summary: Contrary to the central claim (Hsu, 2026) published in Physics Letters B, the Tomonaga--Schwinger equation remains covariant despite the nonlinear modification of it. The proof of covariance becomes simple after the loopholes and mistakes in Hsu's arguments are identified.

AI.tldr: The paper refutes Hsu's (2026) claim that the Tomonaga-Schwinger equation loses covariance under nonlinear modification, demonstrating that the equation remains covariant and identifying errors in Hsu's arguments.
AI.motivation: To correct the erroneous claim by Hsu (2026) in Physics Letters B that the Tomonaga-Schwinger equation loses covariance when nonlinearly modified, and to provide a proper understanding of the equation's covariance properties.
AI.method: Analysis of Hsu's arguments to identify loopholes and mistakes, followed by a simplified proof demonstrating the covariance of the Tomonaga-Schwinger equation under nonlinear modification.
