AI.result: The Tomonaga-Schwinger equation remains covariant despite nonlinear modifications, contrary to Hsu's claim. The proof of covariance becomes straightforward once the errors in Hsu's reasoning are identified.
AI.conclusion: Hsu's (2026) claim about loss of covariance in the nonlinear Tomonaga-Schwinger equation is incorrect; the equation maintains its covariance properties, and the errors in Hsu's arguments have been clearly identified and corrected.

title: Consensus Protocols for Entanglement-Aware Scheduling in Distributed Quantum Neural Networks
summary: The realization of distributed quantum neural networks (DQNNs) over quantum internet infrastructures faces fundamental challenges arising from the fragile nature of entanglement and the demanding synchronization requirements of distributed learning. We introduce a Consensus-Entanglement-Aware Scheduling (CEAS) framework that co-designs quantum consensus protocols with adaptive entanglement management to enable robust synchronous training across distributed quantum processors. CEAS integrates fidelity-weighted aggregation, in which parameter updates are weighted by quantum Fisher information to suppress noisy contributions, with decoherence-aware entanglement scheduling that treats Bell pairs as perishable resources subject to exponential decay. The framework incorporates quantum-authenticated Byzantine fault tolerance, ensuring security against malicious nodes while maintaining compatibility with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) constraints. Our theoretical analysis establishes convergence guarantees under heterogeneous noise conditions, while numerical simulations demonstrate that CEAS maintains 10-15 percentage points higher accuracy compared to entanglement-oblivious baselines under coordinated Byzantine attacks, achieving 90 percent Bell-pair utilization despite coherence time limitations. This work provides a foundational architecture for scalable distributed quantum machine learning, bridging quantum networking, distributed optimization, and early fault-tolerant quantum computation.

AI.tldr: CEAS framework co-designs quantum consensus protocols with adaptive entanglement management for robust distributed quantum neural networks, achieving higher accuracy and better resource utilization under noise and attacks.
AI.motivation: Distributed quantum neural networks face fundamental challenges from fragile entanglement and demanding synchronization requirements in quantum internet infrastructures, requiring robust solutions for distributed learning.
AI.method: Consensus-Entanglement-Aware Scheduling (CEAS) integrates fidelity-weighted aggregation (parameter updates weighted by quantum Fisher information) with decoherence-aware entanglement scheduling (treating Bell pairs as perishable resources), plus quantum-authenticated Byzantine fault tolerance.
AI.result: CEAS maintains 10-15 percentage points higher accuracy than entanglement-oblivious baselines under coordinated Byzantine attacks, achieves 90% Bell-pair utilization despite coherence time limitations, with theoretical convergence guarantees under heterogeneous noise.
AI.conclusion: CEAS provides a foundational architecture for scalable distributed quantum machine learning, bridging quantum networking, distributed optimization, and early fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: The Quantum Sieve Tracer: A Hybrid Framework for Layer-Wise Activation Tracing in Large Language Models
summary: Mechanistic interpretability aims to reverse-engineer the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet separating sparse semantic signals from high-dimensional polysemantic noise remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces the Quantum Sieve Tracer, a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed to characterize factual recall circuits. We implement a modular pipeline that first localizes critical layers using classical causal tracing, then maps specific attention head activations into an exponentially large quantum Hilbert space. Using open-weight models (Meta Llama-3.2-1B and Alibaba Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct), we perform a two-stage analysis that reveals a fundamental architectural divergence. While Qwen's layer 7 circuit functions as a classic Recall Hub, we discover that Llama's layer 9 acts as an Interference Suppression circuit, where ablating the identified heads paradoxically improves factual recall. Our results demonstrate that quantum kernels can distinguish between these constructive (recall) and reductive (suppression) mechanisms, offering a high-resolution tool for analyzing the fine-grained topology of attention.

AI.tldr: Quantum Sieve Tracer: A hybrid quantum-classical framework using quantum Hilbert space mapping to distinguish between recall and suppression circuits in LLMs, revealing architectural differences between Llama and Qwen models.
AI.motivation: Mechanistic interpretability faces challenges in separating sparse semantic signals from high-dimensional polysemantic noise in LLMs, particularly when trying to reverse-engineer factual recall circuits.
AI.method: Hybrid quantum-classical framework with modular pipeline: 1) classical causal tracing to localize critical layers, 2) mapping attention head activations into exponentially large quantum Hilbert space, 3) two-stage analysis on open-weight models (Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct).
AI.result: Revealed fundamental architectural divergence: Qwen's layer 7 functions as classic Recall Hub, while Llama's layer 9 acts as Interference Suppression circuit (ablation paradoxically improves recall). Quantum kernels distinguish between constructive (recall) and reductive (suppression) mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: Quantum Sieve Tracer provides high-resolution tool for analyzing fine-grained topology of attention, demonstrating quantum kernels' ability to distinguish between different circuit mechanisms in LLMs.

title: Symmetry and localisation in causally constrained quantum operator dynamics
summary: This paper explores the connection between causality and many-body dynamics by studying the algebraic structure of tri-partite unitaries ('walls') which permanently arrest local operator spreading in their time-periodic evolution. We show that the resulting causally independent subsystems arise from the invariance of an embedded sub-algebra in the system (ie. a generalised symmetry) that leads to the splitting of operator space into commuting sub-algebras. The commutant structure of the invariant algebra is then used to construct local conserved quantities. Using representation theory of finite matrix algebras, the general form of wall gates is derived as unitary automorphisms. Taking causal independence as a minimal model for non-ergodic dynamics, we study its effect on probes of many-body quantum chaos. We prove an entanglement area-law due to local constraints and we study its stability against projective measurements. In a random ensemble exhibiting causal independence, we compare spectral correlations with the universal (chaotic) ensemble using the spectral form factor. Our results offer a rigorous understanding of locally constrained quantum dynamics from a quantum information perspective.

AI.tldr: Tri-partite unitaries that arrest operator spreading create causally independent subsystems via embedded sub-algebra invariance, leading to local conserved quantities, entanglement area laws, and suppressed quantum chaos signatures.
AI.motivation: To understand the connection between causality and many-body dynamics by studying how certain unitaries permanently arrest local operator spreading, creating causally independent subsystems as a minimal model for non-ergodic dynamics.
AI.method: Analyze algebraic structure of tri-partite unitaries ('walls') using representation theory of finite matrix algebras to derive general form of wall gates as unitary automorphisms; study commutant structure of invariant algebras to construct local conserved quantities; examine entanglement area laws and stability against measurements; compare spectral correlations using spectral form factor in random ensembles.
AI.result: Causally independent subsystems arise from invariance of embedded sub-algebras (generalized symmetries), splitting operator space into commuting sub-algebras; local conserved quantities constructed from commutant structure; entanglement area-law proven due to local constraints; spectral correlations in random ensembles with causal independence differ from universal chaotic ensembles.
AI.conclusion: The work provides rigorous understanding of locally constrained quantum dynamics from quantum information perspective, showing how causal independence from invariant sub-algebras leads to non-ergodic behavior, area-law entanglement, and suppressed chaos signatures.
